Partial Mantel Test

Source: R/mantel.r
mantel_partial.Rd

Tests whether two distance matrices are correlated after removing the effect of a third: for instance, whether samples with more different communities are also more different in pH, beyond what geographic distance between them explains. Gives the same statistic as vegan::mantel.partial() (Pearson, Spearman, or Kendall partial correlation), with permutation p-values, computed in parallel C straight from the distances. mantel() is the simple Mantel test.

Usage

mantel_partial(
  dm,
  y,
  given,
  data = NULL,
  method = "pearson",
  permutations = 999L,
  strata = NULL,
  alternative = "greater",
  seed = 0L,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

dm

A dist object, such as from beta_div() or bray(), or a symmetric numeric matrix of distances. Must not contain NAs or negative values. Its samples are the ones permuted.

y

The distances to correlate with dm: a dist object or a symmetric numeric matrix, like dm, matched to dm's samples by name when both have names, otherwise in the same order. Or numeric values, such as age or pH, whose absolute differences (as stats::dist(y)) are the distances: with data, the name of one of its numeric columns or a vector with one value per row of data; without data, a vector with one value per sample, matched to the samples by name when it has names, otherwise in the same order.

given

The distances whose effect is removed from the correlation of dm and y, as vegan::mantel.partial()'s zdis: such as geographic distances between the samples. Given in any of the forms y takes, including as a column name of data. Required.

data

Optional sample metadata: a data frame with one row per sample, whose columns y, given, and strata can name. Rows are matched to the samples in dm by row name, and rows for other samples are ignored; without row names, they must be in the same order as dm. Default: NULL.

method

The correlation coefficient: 'pearson', 'spearman', or 'kendall' (tau-b), as in stats::cor(). Default: 'pearson'.

permutations

The number of permutations. Default: 999. Alternatively, a matrix with one permutation of 1:n per row, as from permute::shuffleSet(), to use instead of random ones.

strata

Permute samples only within these groups (blocks), for designs such as repeated measures. With data, the name of one of its columns, or a vector with one value per row of data. Without data, a vector with one value per sample, matched to the samples by name when it has names, otherwise in the same order. Default: NULL (free permutation).

alternative

Which correlations count as more extreme than the observed one: 'greater' (more positive, as in vegan::mantel()), 'less' (more negative), or 'two.sided' (larger in absolute value). Default: 'greater'.

seed

An integer seed for the random permutations. The same seed gives the same p-values. Default: 0

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), is the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it. Results are the same for any cpus.

Value

A list of class c('ecodive_mantel', 'ecodive_test'), as from mantel(), with:

  • statistic: The partial Mantel statistic, c(r = ...): the partial correlation of dm and y given given. vegan::mantel.partial()'s statistic.

  • p_value: The permutation p-value.

  • z: The standardized effect size, (r - mean(r_perm)) / sd(r_perm).

  • n_perm: The number of permutations.

  • method: The correlation coefficient: 'pearson', 'spearman', or 'kendall'.

  • alternative: 'greater', 'less', or 'two.sided'.

  • partial: TRUE.

  • n: The number of samples.

  • permutation: How samples were permuted: 'free', 'within strata', or 'supplied matrix'.

Attribute r_perm is a vector of the statistics of the permutations, as vegan::mantel.partial()'s perm. as.data.frame() gives the main results as one row, with test = 'mantel_partial'.

Details

Method

The partial Mantel test (Smouse et al. 1986; Legendre & Legendre 2012) correlates the \(n(n-1)/2\) distances of dm (\(x\)) and y after removing the effect of given (\(z\)), as the partial correlation $$r_{xy.z} = \frac{r_{xy} - r_{xz} r_{yz}}{\sqrt{1 - r_{xz}^2} \sqrt{1 - r_{yz}^2}}$$ where each \(r\) is the Pearson, Spearman, or Kendall correlation of two sets of distances. As in vegan::mantel.partial(), the p-value comes from permutations of the samples of dm, with y and given held fixed: \(r_{xy}\) and \(r_{xz}\) are recomputed for each permutation, and \(r_{yz}\) is computed once. The p-value is the proportion of permutations, counting the observed one, with a partial correlation at least as extreme, as in mantel().

Its p-values can be too small when the distances are spatially autocorrelated (Legendre & Fortin 2010; Guillot & Rousset 2013).

When y and given, or dm and given, are perfectly correlated, there is no partial correlation: the statistic and p-value are NA, with a warning.

Speed, memory, and reproducibility

As for mantel(): each permutation is one pass over the distances (two correlations, \(r_{xy}\) and \(r_{xz}\), in the same pass), with no \(n \times n\) matrix, and permutations run in parallel. They come from seed, so p-values are identical from run to run and for any number of cpus, and agree with vegan::mantel.partial()'s exactly when the same permutations matrix is given to both.

Differences from vegan::mantel.partial()

  • y and given may also be numeric vectors, one value per sample, or names of columns of data.

  • Samples are matched by name between dm, y, given, data, and strata.

  • alternative adds lower-tail and two-sided tests.

  • There's no na.rm: distances must not be NA.

References

Guillot, G., & Rousset, F. (2013). Dismantling the Mantel tests. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 4(4), 336-344. doi:10.1111/2041-210x.12018

Legendre, P., & Fortin, M.-J. (2010). Comparison of the Mantel test and alternative approaches for detecting complex multivariate relationships in the spatial analysis of genetic data. Molecular Ecology Resources, 10(5), 831-844. doi:10.1111/j.1755-0998.2010.02866.x

Legendre, P., & Legendre, L. (2012). Numerical Ecology (3rd ed.), section 10.5. Elsevier.

Smouse, P. E., Long, J. C., & Sokal, R. R. (1986). Multiple regression and correlation extensions of the Mantel test of matrix correspondence. Systematic Zoology, 35(4), 627-632. doi:10.2307/2413122

See also

mantel(), mantel_correlogram(), mantel_regression(), dist_test(), beta_div()

Examples

    # 30 samples along a pH gradient, which shifts the first five genera,
    # at random locations.
    set.seed(1)
    counts <- matrix(rpois(30 * 20, 5), 30, 20)
    rownames(counts) <- paste0('S', 1:30)
    meta <- data.frame(
      row.names = rownames(counts),
      ph  = round(runif(30, 6, 8), 1),
      lat = runif(30, 30, 35),
      lon = runif(30, -100, -95) )
    counts[, 1:5] <- counts[, 1:5] + round(4 * (meta$ph - 6))

    dm  <- bray(counts)
    geo <- dist(meta[, c('lat', 'lon')])

    # Are samples that differ more in pH also more different in
    # community composition, beyond the effect of geographic distance?
    mantel_partial(dm, 'ph', given = geo, data = meta)
#> Partial Mantel test (Pearson) of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity
#> 
#> r = 0.5931, p = 0.001, z = 9.759
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Correlation: Pearson's product-moment correlation
#> Alternative: greater (r is more positive than by chance)
#> Samples: 30

    # With rank correlation.
    mantel_partial(dm, 'ph', given = geo, data = meta, method = 'spearman')
#> Partial Mantel test (Spearman) of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity
#> 
#> r = 0.5528, p = 0.001, z = 9.969
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Correlation: Spearman's rank correlation rho
#> Alternative: greater (r is more positive than by chance)
#> Samples: 30

    # The same, through dist_test().
    dist_test(dm, 'mantel_partial', 'ph', meta, given = geo, method = 'spearman')
#> Partial Mantel test (Spearman) of Bray-Curtis Dissimilarity
#> 
#> r = 0.5528, p = 0.001, z = 9.969
#> Permutations: 999 (free)
#> 
#> Correlation: Spearman's rank correlation rho
#> Alternative: greater (r is more positive than by chance)
#> Samples: 30
